skill.name: drizzle-orm-patterns
skill.description: Comprehensive Drizzle ORM guidance for PostgreSQL projects, including edge runtime setup, migrations, queries, relations, transactions, performance, and type-safe patterns.
skill.summary: Apply production-ready Drizzle ORM patterns for PostgreSQL and Vercel Edge Runtime applications.
skill.author: Barnhardt-Enterprises-Inc

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer produced many high-severity hits, but the reviewed evidence is documentation, ORM examples, or validator pattern strings rather than executable malicious behavior. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, destructive automation, or covert network behavior was found in the provided static evidence.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes placeholder database URLs and environment variable examples.
remediation.suggestion: Keep credentials clearly marked as placeholders and remind users never to commit real connection strings.

remediation.issue: The validator accepts file patterns and expands globs.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the validator should be run only on trusted local paths or staged project files.

remediation.issue: Several SQL template examples are intentionally flagged by simple pattern scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label unsafe examples and safe alternatives clearly so users can distinguish warnings from recommended code.

content.value_statement: Database code often loses type safety when projects add migrations, relations, and raw SQL. This skill gives Claude and Codex practical Drizzle ORM patterns for PostgreSQL and edge deployments.
actual_capabilities: Explains Drizzle ORM setup for PostgreSQL and Neon connections.
Provides migration patterns for safe schema changes and backfills.
Shows query, relation, and transaction examples with TypeScript types.
Highlights performance practices for selects, joins, batching, and indexes.
Includes a local query validator for common unsafe Drizzle patterns.
limitations: Focuses on PostgreSQL and Drizzle ORM rather than every SQL database.
Examples require adaptation to each project schema and naming style.
The validator is heuristic and cannot prove every query is safe.
It does not run migrations or connect to a database by itself.

use_cases.title: Create a Drizzle schema
use_cases.description: Design tables, relations, indexes, and inferred TypeScript types for a PostgreSQL feature.

use_cases.title: Review a migration plan
use_cases.description: Check schema changes, backfills, and rollback steps before applying them to production.

use_cases.title: Improve query performance
use_cases.description: Refactor slow Drizzle queries with selected fields, joins, batching, indexes, and caching guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Drizzle schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the drizzle-orm-patterns skill to design a PostgreSQL Drizzle schema for users, organizations, and memberships. Include relations and inferred insert and select types.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a query safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the drizzle-orm-patterns skill to rewrite this Drizzle query so it avoids unsafe raw SQL, selects only needed fields, and keeps TypeScript inference clear.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the drizzle-orm-patterns skill to plan a zero-downtime migration that adds a non-null column, backfills existing rows, and includes verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit database access patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the drizzle-orm-patterns skill to audit my Drizzle data layer for N+1 queries, unsafe SQL templates, transaction issues, and edge runtime compatibility.

output_examples.input: Design a Drizzle schema for posts, authors, and comments.
output: A normalized table plan with primary keys and foreign keys.
Relation guidance for author to posts and post to comments.
Type inference notes for inserts and query results.

output_examples.input: Review this migration that adds a required profile field.
output: Warnings about locks, defaults, and rollback limits.

output_examples.input: Find performance problems in these Drizzle queries.
output: A list of likely N+1 and over-select patterns.
Suggested joins, projections, and index changes.
Notes on when caching or batching is appropriate.

best_practices: Prefer Drizzle query builders and placeholders before raw SQL fragments.
Run migration plans in stages when changing existing production data.
Select only required columns and verify indexes for frequent filters.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real database URLs or Redis tokens into prompts or examples.
Do not use raw SQL interpolation for untrusted values.
Do not run generated migrations against production without review and backup planning.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce safer Drizzle ORM schemas, queries, migrations, and performance reviews.

faq.question: Does it support databases other than PostgreSQL?
faq.answer: The guidance is centered on PostgreSQL. Some Drizzle concepts may transfer, but examples may need changes.

faq.question: Can it run migrations for me?
faq.answer: No. It can plan and review migration steps, but users must run database commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Is it safe to include production secrets?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholder values and never paste real database URLs, tokens, or credentials into prompts.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can the validator catch every unsafe query?
faq.answer: No. It checks common patterns, but human review and tests are still needed for security and correctness.
